match.reason: No existing point covers marketing objectives; the closest, vision, mission and goals, is about whole-business goals in general rather than measurable goals set for marketing.

draft.title: Marketing objectives
card: A marketing objective is a goal for what the marketing will achieve. It is set after the business has looked at where it stands now.
A good objective is measurable and has a time limit. For example: raise market share from 12% to 17% within one year.
Market share is the percentage of total sales in a market that one business makes. Other objectives can aim at sales volume, profit or the number of customers.
Objectives come first. Marketing strategies are then designed to meet them, and results can be compared with the objective to see if it was met.
draft.remember: An objective says what the marketing must achieve, in numbers and by a date. Strategies are chosen to meet it.

a.q: Which of these is the best marketing objective for a bakery?
opts: Raise sales by 8% over the next 12 months
Become a much more popular bakery
Run more advertising on social media
Offer a new range of sourdough loaves
a.why: It gives a measurable target and a time limit, so results can be checked against it. The popularity option has no number or date. The advertising and sourdough options are strategies, which are ways of meeting an objective, not the goal itself.
a.clue: Which one has both a number and a time limit?

b.q: Priya owns a gym in Newcastle. She wants to gain 150 new members by the end of June. A year later, how should she use this goal?
opts: Compare the actual new members with 150 to judge results
Treat it as a strategy, such as a free trial month
Replace it with a goal that has no number or date
Choose it after deciding which strategies to use
b.why: The target is measurable, so she can compare actual new members with 150 and see if the objective was met. A free trial month would be a strategy to meet the goal, not the goal. The objective is set first, so strategies are designed to meet it, not the other way round.
b.clue: A number and a date make a goal something you can check.

problems.detail: The remember line says an objective says what the marketing 'must' achieve. The card only says it is a goal for what the marketing 'will' achieve, and that results 'can' be compared. The remember line also says every objective is 'in numbers and by a date', while the card says this is what makes a good objective.

The timing is confusing. The goal is 'by the end of June', but the question asks what to do 'a year later' without saying a year after what. Something like 'In July, how should she use this goal?' would be clearer.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer and the facts are correct. The remember line uses 'must' and treats every objective as having a number and a date, which is stronger than the card, and question b's 'a year later' timing is unclear.
